claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A machine-learned interatomic potential can be integrated with physical constraints and calibrated using tensile and fracture-test data.
The proposed potential can predict complete stress-strain responses, Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
The framework will be evaluated at room temperature under controlled tensile loading.
Fracture behavior will be evaluated under standardized conditions such as single-edge-notched bending.
The calibrated potential will capture the alloy's local multiscale chemical heterogeneities and bond distortions.
Capturing local heterogeneities and bond distortions will mediate accurate stress and strain predictions.
Embedding physical constraints in the learned potential prevents overfitting.
Preventing overfitting through physical constraints improves generalization to complex deformation modes.
A machine-learned potential can reduce computational overhead relative to direct first-principles calculations.
The proposed method will provide at least a tenfold reduction in computation time.
The proposed method will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 20–30% over first-principles, CALPHAD, or standard machine-learning approaches.
First-principles and related atomistic methods impose high computational demands that impede high-throughput alloy searches.
CALPHAD can require significant computational resources and can be limited by the lack of reliable high-entropy-alloy databases.
Machine-learning models can predict mechanical properties, including yield strength, with reasonable or high accuracy.
The reliability of machine-learning predictions depends on the size, composition, quality, and representativeness of the training data.
The proposed potential may become unreliable at high temperatures, under extreme loading, or otherwise outside its training regime.
The potential may become unreliable if the alloy microstructure differs substantially from the reported hierarchical state.
Failure to achieve both the stated tenfold efficiency gain and the stated 20–30% accuracy improvement against experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
